thread:
carol: FYI we've been seeing repeated microburst egress events on a handful of dedicated slices in eu-west-1. Not full saturation but enough to flip allocator decisions and trigger warm pool churn.

carol: pattern: 100-700ms blasts, ~40-120MB per burst, often at model rollback windows. Makes SLOs noisy.

jorge: are these tenant-driven or an app-level fanout? any correlation with batching params?

carol: looks tenant-driven. Traces show single tenant with many parallel short calls (client-side fanout). Batching didn't help because bursts are at L4 level.

leah: proposal: leaky-bucket pacing at the node edge (host proxy) per-tenant, with overflow routing to a shared egress gateway that has larger NIC headroom. Host-level avoids allocator moves.

jorge: curious about host vs cluster-proxy tradeoffs. Host gives immediate control but harder to rollout. Cluster proxy centralizes logic but adds hop.

leah: tradeoffs: host-proxy keeps routing local -> lower extra latency on normal ops. cluster-proxy fallback allows global shaping and easier billing attribution. thinking: dual-mode: host token-bucket for steady-state + cluster fallback when host escrow exhausted.

carol: we need a cost cap. Fallback gateway could incur cross-AZ egress or warm-pool compute. We should expose a tenant-level budget and a kill-switch that drops overflow when budget exceeded.

jorge: +1. also need to preserve model fidelity when routing to fallback: route only to equivalent-quantized models or same-arch variants. can't silently degrade customer quality.

leah: rough config idea:

```
host_proxy:
  tenant_pacing:
    mode: "leaky_bucket"
    rate_mb_s: 100
    burst_mb: 64
    refill_interval_ms: 200
    overflow: "cluster_fallback" # options: drop, cluster_fallback
    overflow_budget_header: "X-Tenant-Egress-Budget"

cluster_gateway:
  accept_fallbacks: true
  routing_policy: "compatible_model_only"
  budget_enforcement: true
```

jorge: metrics we need: host_escrow_used, host_overflow_count, fallback_routed_count, fallback_cost_charge, escalated_allocator_moves (should go down).

carol: let's define canary: enable host pacing on 2 racks (r-eu1a, r-eu1b) for 72h, with cluster_fallback disabled initially (so we see local shaping only). If p99 latency and allocator churn drop -> enable fallback in a second phase with budget checks on.

leah: operational checklist:
- add telemetry + histogram for burst size distribution
- add tenant budget header surface for billing team
- create runbook steps for fallback kill-switch and warm-pool routing verification

infra-bot: canary schedule queued: phase1 -> host-only on racks r-eu1a,r-eu1b starting 2025-04-22T03:00Z for 72h. Will post updates to #eng-sre.

jorge: one more thing: ensure no false positives from our burst detector during deploy windows. we should exclude deploy traffic by default.

carol: good call. add exclude tag for deploys and Canary traffic.

leah: I can produce a PR for host_proxy pacing by EOD. Will include unit tests that simulate burst floods and assert allocator moves don't increase.

jorge: I'll work with billing to spec the budget header and cost signals.

carol: assigning follow-ups: leah -> host_proxy PR + tests; jorge -> billing hooks + metrics dashboard; carol -> runbook + canary monitor. Sync tomorrow 09:30 UTC.

carol: objections?

jorge: none. :thumbsup:

leah: LGTM.

carol: thanks, deploying the canary plan once PR lands.
